newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends firmer, talk of more bond issues.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends firmer, talk of more bond issues.

text.p: Talk of more Kiwi/samurai bond issues helped the New Zealand dollar up at Monday's close, assisted by buying interest out of Singapore, dealers said.
The Kiwi finished at US$0.6935/42 from 0.6923/30 at the opening, having traded a 0.6917-36 range on the day.
The Trade-Weighted Index ended at 69.16, up strongly from 68.89 at the open.
There was also speculation of more Kiwi/samurai bonds after the latest World Bank NZ$100 million launch over the weekend.
"It is closing better bid and the underlying trend seems to be coming from overseas," one dealer said.
"With this World Bank issue there is obviously still interest," he added.
But the Kiwi was expected to struggle to get through resistance at $0.6950, especially after the weekend G7 meeting and the ensuing push higher by dollar/yen and dollar/mark.
Such a scenario would push the TWI up to near the top of its threshold and see the Kiwi/U.S. ratchet down in response, another senior dealer said.
